probe_evidence:
VERIFIED. This is the one category where "availability not assortment" does NOT hold — the assortment is genuinely, measurably absent, and probe CONFIRMED the "missing" verdicts instead of overturning them.

Method: 51 researched lines re-probed individually with `ary assort probe` using 4-8 molecule + brand variants each, plus one raw SQL sweep OR-ing 267 molecule/brand tokens as LIKE substrings across all 21,479 SKUs (19,494 active), 12m window 2025-09-01..2026-08-31 (DB live to 2026-08-30, `ary doctor`).

HARD ZERO — no SKU exists anywhere in the catalogue, under any group:
metformin/glycomet/gluconorm; glimepiride/gemer/amaryl; sitagliptin/vildagliptin/dapagliflozin/empagliflozin; voglibose/pioglitazone; semaglutide/rybelsus; insulin (all forms, human + analogue); pen needles/syringes; glucometer/accuchek/onetouch/contour; lancets/softclix; telmisartan/telma; losartan/olmesartan; amlodipine/amlong/stamlo; metoprolol/atenolol/bisoprolol/nebivolol; ramipril/enalapril; chlorthalidone/torsemide/furosemide/spironolactone; atorvastatin/rosuvastatin; clopidogrel; sorbitrate/nitroglycerin; BP monitor/omron/sphygmo; levothyroxine/thyronorm/eltroxin; carbimazole; salbutamol/asthalin/ventolin/rotacap; respules/levosalbutamol/ipratropium; budesonide/budecort/fluticasone; seroflo/foracort/formoterol; montelukast/montek; theophylline/deriphyllin; prednisolone/omnacortil/wysolone; nasal steroid/nasonex/flomist; levocetirizine/cetirizine/fexofenadine/avil; spacer/zerostat; nebuliser/oximeter/peak-flow; amoxicillin/augmentin/clavam; azithromycin/azithral/azee; cefixime/cefuroxime/cephalexin; doxycycline; nitrofurantoin; metronidazole/ornidazole/ofloxacin; levofloxacin/ciprofloxacin; mupirocin/soframycin/betadine/neosporin; levetiracetam/valproate/carbamazepine/phenytoin; pantoprazole/omeprazole/rabeprazole; ferrous/folic/autrin/dexorange.

THE COVERAGE DIFF IS UNUSABLE — it is wrong in the OPPOSITE direction to the usual trap, understating the gap. It claims 24.5% coverage / 31 "covered" + 8 "dormant" lines. 30 of the 31 and 8 of the 8 are bad substring matches:
- "DPP-4 FDCs", "SGLT2" and "nebuliser machine" all matched `%500%` → the same 559 SKUs / Rs 17.99 L of 500ml water and 500g packs.
- "ICS+LABA inhaler" matched `%250%` → 454 SKUs / Rs 22.01 L.
- "Glucometer starter kit" matched `%active%` → Colgate Active Salt, Surf Excel Active Hygiene, Huggies Active Baby, Real Active juice (VERIFIED by listing all 12).
- "Beta blockers" matched `%concor%` → exactly one SKU: `01LN Concord Kadai 05 03`, Cookware (VERIFIED).
- "Acid suppression / PPI" matched `%razo%` → 12 Gillette/Laser razors + Hart Beat "Corazon" candy (VERIFIED by listing).
- "CGM sensor" matched `%libre%` → Calibre Scale 30cm, Stationery (VERIFIED).
- Also garbage: "plus", "oral", "other", "pain", "spray", "syrup", "drops", "digital", "needles", "premix", "odin", "leo", "cipla", "180", "750", "192", "203", "116", "114", "139".
TRUE coverage is 1 line of 51 (2.0%), not 24.5%.

The three states, separated:
(c) COVERED — 1 line: sugar substitutes / diabetic sweeteners. 25 SKUs, 12 selling, Rs 74,282 (Zydus Sugar Free Gold/Natura/Stevia, Sugarlite). Do not touch.
PARTIAL — 1 line: ORS. 5 ready-to-drink bottles (Cipla ORS 200ml x3 flavours + generic orange/apple), Rs 8,161, filed under Soft Drinks -> Packed Juice. The WHO-formula sachet and zinc dispersible are ZERO.
(b) LISTED BUT DORMANT — no complete line, only 6 stray SKUs, and the provenance query kills them: `01J4`/`01J5` Cipla Thermometer and `02BA` Hicks Thermometer have ZERO purchase bills EVER, ZERO stock, ZERO sales EVER — pure catalogue paperwork, never once bought. GSK Ostocalcium 200ml + Total 30N last purchased 2023; Avomine (promethazine, Schedule H) last purchased 19-Dec-2023.
(a) GENUINELY ABSENT — 49 of 51 lines. Sized below.

What ARY actually sells that is allopathic, ALL of it, 12m: 19 SKUs, ~769 bills, Rs 41,454 = 0.0542% of the Rs 7.65 Cr turnover and 0.21% of 372,336 bills. Benadryl 150/60ml Rs 12,372; Strepsils Rs 7,325; Omnigel Rs 4,910; Volini Rs 5,707; ORS RTD Rs 8,161; Disprin Rs 907; Paracitamol 500 Rs 590; Crocin 500 Rs 502; D-Cold Rs 558; Otrivin Rs 352; Cofsils Rs 70.

Nested availability failure inside the absent assortment (this is the part that would repeat): 7 of those 19 are at ZERO stock right now. Crocin 500 was purchased ONCE in the shop's history (25 strips, 21-Nov-2025), sold out by 14-Feb-2026, stock 0, never reordered in six months.

Correction to the vault: [[Pharmacy]] and [[Gap-List]] say "26 strips of paracetamol in twelve months". Live 12m is Crocin 26 + Paracitamol 500 generic 59 + Disprin 120 = 205 units across 187 bills — still trivial for 4,700 people, but ~8x the quoted figure. Second correction: [[Pharmacy]] says ExpDate is "populated on ZERO of 111,021 rows". Live it is populated on ALL 111,253 rows of both ProductChildMaster and ProductChildDetail — with the sentinel 1900-01-01 on every single one, 0 rows above 2000-01-01. Same conclusion, different mechanism: the field EXISTS and has never once been used, so this is a configuration/process project, not a software absence.

The whole 272-SKU Medicare group (group 138) was read line by line: churan, chyawanprash, Dettol, Vicks, Moov, Eno, glucose powder, mosquito coils, badam roghan, 3 dead thermometers. Not one prescription drug. Group does Rs 3.13 L = Rs 67/resident/yr.
penetration_assumption:
Split into two tranches with different blocker profiles. Every input below is ESTIMATED unless marked VERIFIED; the disease-prevalence rates and the hospital's free-dispensing share are NOT-CHECKED against any live source and are the softest numbers here.

Population base (vault [[Population]], externally VERIFIED, not re-checked by me): ~4,550-4,800 term-time; permanent winter core 1,700-2,300 measured three ways off ARY's own till. Composition: EU students 1,102 + Akal Academy ~1,250 + School of Spiritual Sciences 305 = ~2,650 students/children with near-zero chronic Rx demand; adults are EU faculty+staff 145, AIRWE 487, resident staff families ~700-1,300. Call it ~2,050 adults.

TRANCHE A — devices and diagnostics, no Schedule H drugs. Rs 2.40 L/yr, fully incremental (VERIFIED: current device sales = Rs 0).
- "Of ~2,050 resident adults, ~150 are diagnosed diabetic (7-8% of adults, deliberately below the 10-12% Indian urban figure because this cohort skews younger and rural). 20% buy a meter in year one at Rs 1,100; 50 people then test twice weekly = 96 strips/yr at Rs 15." -> meters Rs 33k + strips Rs 72k + lancets Rs 12.5k = Rs 1.00 L.
- "~350 resident adults are diagnosed hypertensive (17% of adults). 8% buy a digital upper-arm monitor in year one at Rs 1,700." -> Rs 0.40 L.
- "4,700 residents in ~1,000 households and hostel units buy 150 thermometers/yr at Rs 180, 40 pulse oximeters at Rs 900, and Rs 40k of first-aid consumables." -> Rs 1.00 L. Discounted hard, because ARY has already listed 3 thermometers and never once bought them.

TRANCHE B — licensed retail pharmacy (Form 20/21). Rs 14.3 L gross, Rs 13.3 L incremental after ~Rs 1.0 L of existing allopathic OTC relocates off the Medicare shelf.
- B1 acute/OTC allopathic: "each of 4,700 residents buys an acute-illness item 2.5 times a year at a Rs 55 ticket" -> Rs 6.46 L, taken at Rs 6.0 L. Sanity check: Rs 128/resident/yr, against the live comparator of sanitary pads at Rs 98/resident/yr (VERIFIED: 30 SKUs, all 30 selling, Rs 4.92 L) — the one health category ARY stocks properly, and proof the model works here when the range exists.
- B2 chronic Rx refills: "~450 distinct chronic patients (diabetes + BP + thyroid, net of overlap) among resident adults. Akal Charitable Hospital dispenses free on the same campus, so only 30% buy retail — for brand preference, convenience, weekends/nights, or a molecule off the free formulary. 135 patients x Rs 380/month x 12." -> Rs 6.16 L, taken at Rs 6.0 L. Rs 380/month is a 2-3 drug generic-brand regimen (metformin + telmisartan + atorvastatin).
- B3 antibiotics/short-course Rx: "4,700 residents x 0.35 courses/yr reaching retail rather than free OPD x Rs 150/course" -> Rs 2.47 L, taken at Rs 2.3 L.

TOTAL INCREMENTAL REVENUE Rs 15.7 L/yr = Rs 334/resident/yr = 2.1% of ARY's Rs 7.65 Cr (VERIFIED: 372,336 bills / 354 trading days / Rs 205.56 basket). That is a 5x step on the health shelf from Rs 67/resident/yr today, and ~3.4x the sanitary-pad benchmark — defensible for opening a licensed department where none exists, and deliberately ~78% below a normal Indian per-capita retail-medicine spend because of the free hospital and the young cohort.

MARGIN — I could NOT derive drug margin from ARY's purchase ledger, because ARY has never bought a drug: zero purchase bills from any pharma distributor in the shop's history, and the one account named "Medicare Surgicals" (AccountID 2061) has never been used for a single purchase (VERIFIED). Current health suppliers are FMCG wholesalers (Baghat Enterprises, Himachal Wholesale Syndicate, Solan Agencies).
What I DID derive live from PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost vs SaleDetail.SaleRate, same 12m window: Medicare group GM = 26.17% on Rs 3.13 L across 87 costed SKUs; shop-wide GM = 22.19% on Rs 6.42 Cr across 4,767 costed SKUs. VERIFIED, both.
- Tranche A at 22.19% (devices are ordinary traded goods, not DPCO-capped) = Rs 0.53 L.
- Tranche B at 19% blended — ASSUMED, not derived: DPCO 2013 caps scheduled-formulation retailer margin at 16% (vault, research-lane VERIFIED against HP sources, not re-checked by me), ~21% on non-scheduled, at a 40/60 scheduled/non-scheduled mix — = Rs 2.53 L, less 3% of sales as expiry write-off (Rs 0.40 L) = Rs 2.13 L. The write-off is at the pessimistic end deliberately, because there is zero batch/expiry discipline to control it.
TOTAL GROSS MARGIN Rs 2.66 L/yr.

THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE REVENUE: Rs 2.66 L of gross margin against a mandatory dedicated registered-pharmacist FTE at Rs 2.16-3.00 L/yr. Contribution before rent, shrink, capital cost and the ERP work is minus Rs 0.34 L to plus Rs 0.50 L. On the central case the pharmacy does not reliably clear its own pharmacist. It becomes clearly worth doing only if the hospital hosts or shares the licence and the pharmacist (killing that whole line), or if the hospital's free formulary is narrower than the 70% assumed, or if the ~44,000-48,000 outside OPD visits/year the hospital pulls in — footfall that is NOT in the 4,700 and is currently uncounted — are counted as catchment.

One argument I checked and could NOT support: "a pharmacy is counter-seasonal, it survives the winter shutdown". ARY's existing health shelf falls HARDER than the shop — Medicare Jan-2026 is 54% of Nov-2025, the shop is 63% (VERIFIED, monthly series). Today's shelf is student-driven cough/cold impulse. A chronic shelf would plausibly behave differently, but nothing in this data says so, so it is not in the number.
top_skus: Paracetamol 500/650 (Crocin, Dolo 650, Calpol) — restock and hold: ARY bought Crocin ONCE ever (25 strips, 21-Nov-2025), sold out 14-Feb-2026, stock 0 today, never reordered
Glucometer + test strips (Accu-Chek Active / Dr Morepen Gluco One BG-03) — highest-value device line, no Schedule H, hard zero in the catalogue
Digital upper-arm BP monitor + large cuff (Omron / Dr Morepen) — hard zero; ~350 diagnosed hypertensive adults on campus and no monitor within 30-50 km
ORS WHO-formula sachets (Electral / ORS-L) + zinc dispersible — the ready-to-drink bottle already sells Rs 8,161, the sachet and zinc are absent
Digital thermometer — 3 listed since inception with ZERO purchase bills EVER; buy the ones already on the catalogue before adding new lines
Antacid + PPI: Digene/Gelusil tablets, pantoprazole 40mg, rabeprazole — zero antacid tablet anywhere in 21,479 SKUs
Metformin 500 IR/SR and 1g (Glycomet, Gluconorm SR) — the anchor chronic molecule in India; hard zero
Telmisartan 40 + amlodipine 5 (Telma, Amlong/Stamlo), plain and +HCTZ — the two anchor BP molecules; hard zero
Levothyroxine full strength ladder 25/50/75/100 mcg (Thyronorm, Eltroxin) — hard zero, and hypothyroidism is common in HP hill populations
Salbutamol MDI reliever + spacer (Asthalin, Zerostat) — hard zero; an asthma reliever is a life-safety item on a campus with ~2,650 boarding students
blockers: PHARMACIST FTE IS LARGER THAN THE PRIZE — the single deciding blocker. HP requires a registered pharmacist (HP Pharmacy Council, Shimla) who swears an affidavit they are not engaged in any other service or business, i.e. a dedicated FTE, not a shared name. Rural Sirmaur cost Rs 18-25k/month = Rs 2.16-3.00 L/yr against a projected Rs 2.66 L of total gross margin. Do not proceed on the standalone economics; proceed only if Akal Hospital hosts/shares the licence and the pharmacist.

AKAL CHARITABLE HOSPITAL DISPENSES FREE ON THE SAME CAMPUS — 100 beds, 11 doctors, ~120-131 outside OPD/day (~44-48k free visits/yr). Whatever it gives free is demand retail never sees, and my 70%-suppression assumption on chronic refills is the largest single uncertainty in the number: it can move the answer +/-50% either way. It is one conversation inside the same Trust and it must happen before any money moves. VERIFIED live that the hospital is an ARY customer (00009, Rs 78,210 over 60 bills, 12m) but buys only bedsheets, curtains, room heaters and Vaseline — it sources its own drugs elsewhere, which is consistent with it already holding a licence.

FUSIONERP8 HAS NEVER RECORDED A BATCH OR AN EXPIRY — VERIFIED live: ProductChildMaster and ProductChildDetail both carry ExpDate and MfgDate on all 111,253 rows, every one set to the sentinel 1900-01-01; zero rows above 2000-01-01. The fields exist, so this is a configuration + process project with the vendor rather than a software replacement, but a pharmacy cannot legally trade without batch/expiry for recall, Schedule H1 records and expiry returns to the supplier. Cost and feasibility unknown — ask the vendor before filing Form 19.

DRUG LICENCE — Form 19 under Rule 59(2) for Form 20 + Form 21 (retail). Rs 3,000 challan; site map stamped and signed by the Panchayat Pradhan (rural, 2 originals); board resolution + MOA/AOA of Jivo Wellness Pvt Ltd; Schedule H1 register kept 3 years. Authority: Sirmaur Drug Inspector / DHSR Shimla 0177-2621383. (From the vault's research lane, HP-sourced; I did not re-verify it.) The fee is trivial; the timeline is weeks to months and gates everything else.

NO PHARMA SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH — VERIFIED: zero purchase bills from any pharma distributor in the shop's entire history; the only pharma-sounding account, 'Medicare Surgicals' (2061), has never been used for a single purchase. The Medicare shelf is supplied by FMCG wholesalers (Baghat Enterprises, Himachal Wholesale Syndicate, Solan Agencies, Anchal Trading). A Solan/Nahan/Shimla pharma distributor relationship has to be built from scratch, and the licence is the precondition for it.

EXECUTION RISK, ALREADY PROVEN ON THIS SHOP'S OWN TILL — the three Cipla/Hicks thermometers have ZERO purchase bills EVER, zero stock, zero sales ever: listed and never once bought. And Crocin was bought once, sold out in three months and never reordered; 7 of the 19 allopathic SKUs are at zero stock right now. ARY has already demonstrated it will list a health SKU and never buy it, and will sell out and not replenish. Without a named replenishment owner and a reorder level on every line, this build reverts to paperwork — which is the general 13,284-dead-SKU disease showing up inside the one category where the assortment gap is real.

COLD CHAIN — insulin (human and analogue) needs validated 2-8 degC with a temperature log. ARY runs a Frozen category (60 SKUs, Rs 2.79 L) so there is freezer capacity on site, but not pharma-grade refrigeration with logging. ~Rs 35-60k capex, plus a power-failure plan on a hill campus. Insulin is the one must-have line I would defer to phase two.

CAPITAL AND DEAD-STOCK RISK — Rs 4-6 L of opening stock for a credible chronic + acute range, on a shop whose catalogue already carries 13,284 non-selling SKUs. A chronic range is 3-5 strengths per molecule and most strengths will not move; with no expiry tracking, unsold strengths become write-offs rather than returns.

EXISTING UNLICENSED SALE, today — ARY sells Rs 41,454/yr of allopathic drugs (Benadryl, Strepsils, Omnigel, Volini, Disprin, Crocin, paracetamol, D-Cold, Otrivin) with no Form 20/21, and India has no statutory OTC category, so there is no compliant 'OTC-only corner'. Calibrate it honestly: 0.054% of a Rs 7.65 Cr business, and it is what essentially every kirana in India does. A housekeeping item to fold into the licence decision, not a scandal and not a reason to stop trading.

SEASONALITY IS NOT A HELP — I tested and could not support the 'a pharmacy rides through the winter shutdown' argument. The existing health shelf falls harder than the shop (Medicare Jan-2026 at 54% of Nov-2025 vs the shop's 63%). Term-time student acute demand, which is B1 and the largest single revenue block, drops to near zero for the 23-day vacation floor and the buyer must stop buying ~29 Dec and restart ~20 Jan.
